header.headline: Jokic, Murray help Nuggets hand Pelicans a sixth straight loss

content: NEW ORLEANS (AP)  Nikola Jokic had 26 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists, Jamal Murray added 23 points, seven rebounds and nine assists, and the Denver Nuggets outlasted the New Orleans Pelicans 116-108 on Saturday night.
Denver has won four of its last five games and moved to 3-0 against the Pelicans this season. New Orleans dropped its sixth consecutive contest, four of which have come at home.
Jokic was on triple-double watch, shooting 9 of 14 from the field. Murray shot 9 of 16 and was a team-high +16.

Zion Williamson led New Orleans with 24 points. Saddiq Bey added 16 points, and rookie guard Jaron Pierre Jr. scored 13 in 23 minutes after scoring 23 points for the G-League Laketown Squadron’s inaugural home game earlier Saturday afternoon.

Jokic dictated play early, scoring nine points in the first quarter and entering halftime with 12 points, five rebounds and five assists. But New Orleans showed fight, with Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen combining for 16 points in the first half.
The Pelicans trimmed Denver’s lead to one with 53 seconds left in the half on a Pierre layup, then two on a Karlo Matkovic 3-pointer late in the third quarter.
Christian Braun had 17 points, seven rebounds and four steals for Denver. A spinning DeMar DeRozan jumper gave the Nuggets their largest lead of the night, 102-87, with 6:36 remaining.
Yves Missi (knee) returned to the lineup for New Orleans on a minutes restriction, logging three points, eight rebounds and four blocks after missing the previous 10 games.
Trey Murphy (knee) missed his fourth straight game. Dejounte Murray (ankle) missed his second consecutive game after requesting a trade from the Pelicans on Friday.
Nuggets: Host Phoenix on Monday night.
Pelicans: Host Golden State on Monday night.
See AP’s full NBA coverage here

gameOverview.title: The Denver Nuggets Earn the Win
gameOverview.body:
The Denver Nuggets defeated the New Orleans Pelicans 116-108. Nikola Jokić led the Denver Nuggets with 26 points, 8 rebounds, and 10 assists on 9-for-14 shooting, while Jamal Murray added 23 points with 9 assists. For the New Orleans Pelicans, Zion Williamson scored 24 points on 9-for-16 shooting with 6 rebounds, and Saddiq Bey contributed 16 points, though he shot 4-for-15 from the field.

Denver controlled the early pace and maintained its advantage through halftime. The Pelicans mounted a 12–4 run in the third quarter, but the Nuggets responded decisively with an 18–5 run that spanned the late third and early fourth quarters, extending their lead and seizing control. Christian Braun finished a running dunk that made the score 113–101 in favor of the Nuggets with 0:39.5 remaining in the fourth, effectively closing out the contest. The Denver Nuggets held an edge in paint scoring, while the New Orleans Pelicans had an edge in bench scoring.

Jokić shot 17.1 percentage points above expectation, converting at a higher rate than an average NBA player would be expected to convert the same tracked shot opportunities. Jordan Poole drew above-expected defensive pressure for New Orleans, recording Average Gravity of 11.3, while Jokić's overall impact was reflected in his Total Leverage of 4.1.

definingMoments.title: Jaron Pierre Jr. Finishes the Layup
definingMoments.summary: With 53.7 seconds left in the second, Jaron Pierre Jr. supplied the finish on a layup, and Denver led 52–51.

definingMoments.title: Herbert Jones Delivers a Triple
definingMoments.summary: Herbert Jones hit a three-pointer, and the Nuggets led 52–49 with 1:17 remaining in the second.

definingMoments.title: Trevon Brazile Throws It Down
definingMoments.summary: Trevon Brazile threw down a dunk, and the Nuggets led 15–11 with 5:54 remaining in the first.

topPerformers.summary: Nikola Jokić scored 26 points for the Denver Nuggets, anchoring the offense with consistent scoring production.
Jamal Murray distributed 9 assists for the Denver Nuggets, orchestrating ball movement and creating scoring opportunities.
Jordan Poole of the New Orleans Pelicans generated 2.2 Offensive Leverage, contributing meaningfully to the team's offensive execution across multiple areas.
Christian Braun of the Denver Nuggets recorded 1.6 Defensive Leverage, making credited contributions on the defensive end.

shot_difficulty.homeTeamSummary: Zion Williamson of the New Orleans Pelicans made 9 of 16 field-goal attempts (56.3% from the field), including 2 of 4 from three (50.0% from three). He shot 0.7 percentage points above his expected field-goal percentage of 55.5%.
shot_difficulty.awayTeamSummary: Nikola Jokić converted 9 of 14 attempts at 64.3% from the field, operating well above shot difficulty expectations of 47.2%—a 17.1 percentage point gap. He also made his only three-point attempt at 100.0% from three.

gravity_spotlight.homeSummary: Jordan Poole drew above-expected defensive pressure for the New Orleans Pelicans, posting an average Gravity of 11.3—the team's highest. His 13.8 on-ball perimeter Gravity shows particular attention when handling the ball more than 20 feet from the basket, a significant component of his overall pressure drawn.
gravity_spotlight.awaySummary: Cameron Johnson led the Denver Nuggets in average Gravity at 7.2, drawing above-expected defensive pressure across tracked situations. His 8.4 off-ball perimeter Gravity indicates sustained attention without the ball at distance, anchoring his overall impact on opponent positioning.

homeDefensiveSpotlight.summary: Jeremiah Fears held Christian Braun to 3-for-6 shooting from the field across 6:17 of tracked matchup time. Fears' assignment produced a solid defensive showing against the Denver perimeter threat.

awayDefensiveSpotlight.summary: Nikola Jokić held Derik Queen to 4-for-9 shooting from the field over 6:36 of tracked matchup time. Derik Queen went 2-for-4 from beyond the arc, reflecting a disciplined defensive effort from Nikola Jokić on the New Orleans roster.

homeLeverageSpotlight.summary: Jordan Poole led the New Orleans Pelicans in Total Leverage with 1.8, posting a positive net contribution across measured areas. His 2.2 Creation Leverage reflects credited value from self-created shots, assists and potential assists, anchoring his overall performance.

awayLeverageSpotlight.summary: Nikola Jokić posted 4.1 Total Leverage for the Denver Nuggets, leading the game in that measure. Shooting supplied 2.2 Leverage and creation added 1.9, with both areas contributing to his positive net credited contribution across the measured areas.
